role: independent artifact reviewer; inherited session model; read-only review except this explicitly authorized evidence file
scope: Existing public research artifacts and primary sources; no provider calls, weight downloads, paid generation, asset redistribution or product changes.
verdict: Public TripoSG and commercial Tripo achieving the same quality is not established. The sources do not provide a controlled, paired output of those two systems for the same input, common settings and editable asset contract.

method.selected: Inspect the input, generated and edited visual artifacts directly; verify local bytes and hashes against the existing source manifest; check publisher instructions and paper; separate observations, publisher statements and unverified claims.
rejected_alternatives: Rank unrelated showcase images or treat a polished Blender render as raw model output.
Treat model-card declarations, a generated screenshot, visual similarity, or paper-selected examples as proof of production quality or editable mesh quality.
Require identical numerical settings where systems cannot express them: use a common single-image comparison and disclose a separate optional native-best-settings comparison instead.
method.sandbox: Read-only was an instruction during inspection; runtime was not demonstrated to enforce an OS read-only sandbox. This evidence file is the sole explicitly authorized write.

artifacts.observation: White-background frontal ornamental blue and gold lantern illustration, floral panels, beads and red tassels.

A Tripo interface screenshot shows an angled lantern with dome, patterned panels and hanging tassels. The reference's overall design is recognizable, while the decorations and visible side geometry differ. Screenshot alone does not establish geometry, UV, material layers, topology or editable asset integrity.

A dark final presentation shows bright panels and warm highlights with changed view and lighting. Those changes cannot be isolated from modeling, material or post-processing differences by this image alone.

Eight example input columns, including a person, a bicycle and furniture, and rows labelled TripoSR, CRM, InstantMesh, MeshLRM, MeshFormer, CraftsMan-1.5 and TripoSG. Rendered surface normals show visibly different silhouettes and detail; commercial Tripo is not a row. The normal maps do not demonstrate color or PBR quality.

sources.what_source_says: Tripo Team describes Tripo 3.1/H, Best Quality, 4K texture, triangle and high polycount; the same input image is used for front and back in a multiview workflow, left/right inferred; export to FBX and manual selection/material separation with final lighting in Blender.
sources.limits: Publisher-selected demonstration. Exact revision, seed, polycount, original mesh and reproduction receipt are not established. It is not an isolated controlled comparison of Tripo and Blender or an independent timing test.

sources.what_source_says: Authors report preprocessing the same images by background removal and normal rendering from the same viewpoint for Fig.7 comparisons. They describe TripoSG primarily as textureless shape generation and describe texture generation separately.
sources.limits: Paper figure compares named open models on selected cases; no commercial Tripo row and no independent reproduction in this task. One view does not establish rear geometry, editable topology, or texture quality.

sources.what_source_says: Repository reports a 1.5B image-conditioned release and inference code, a GLB output example, CUDA with at least 8 GB VRAM, automatic weights including RMBG-1.4, and credits FlashVDM.
sources.limits: Commands were not run. Hardware sufficiency in our environment and component rights require separate verification. Repository root license does not settle all component licenses.

sources.what_source_says: Model card describes a single-image, 1.5B-parameter, 2048-latent-token geometry model and requires a CUDA GPU over 8 GB VRAM.
sources.limits: Card and repository requirements have slightly different wording; neither proves actual memory consumption or deployability here.

sources.what_source_says: Tripo credits creator Nano and describes part-based Tripo generation and Blender assembly; it explicitly says the tutorial character images, greeting clip and face close-up are separate demonstration assets.
sources.limits: Do not join those disparate assets into a false before/after comparison. Publisher's creator link https://x.com/Dstudio_ai/status/2096475126942560677 returned HTTP 403 to this reviewer, so original creator artifact was not independently inspected. Public Tripo blog search and this linked creator were explored; no additional independently verified creator before/after pair was established.

direct_benchmark_proposal.purpose: Optional 3D props in a music-first video, while keeping photo optional; no claim of a platform feature or model implementation already completed.

cases.input: Rights-cleared single front image of a clearly bounded solid prop, such as a microphone body; preserve exact file and SHA-256.
cases.focus: silhouette, back-view plausibility, basic textured asset and export.

cases.input: Rights-cleared single front image of a decorative prop with a handle, gaps or thin spokes; preserve exact file and SHA-256.
cases.focus: holes, disconnected pieces, fragile structures, artifact and repair burden.

cases.input: Only if actual subject consents and source/likeness rights permit, use a single authorized portrait or licensed stylized character; image remains optional for the music-first flow.
cases.focus: identity and silhouette consistency across views; static asset only, no unverified claim of rigging or animation.

controlled_conditions: Freeze the exact common single-view input bytes, preprocessing, selection policy and rights records; record each model/provider revision, settings, seed when exposed, output format, and unavailable settings instead of inventing equivalence.

Retain raw unedited output and hashes. If one system cannot emit textures or PBR, record that as a capability difference; assess geometry first and record any independently versioned texturing step separately.

Normalize units, axis, frame and display scale without silently repairing geometry; render front, side and back with identical camera, framing, lighting and normal/material settings. Record raw topology, UVs, material/texture channels, geometry gaps and non-finite data; document any conversions or incompatibilities.

Exercise each supported workflow: admit the owned asset through the platform's actual validation and rights checks; change position, camera and light; attempt supported material edits; save and reopen, approve explicitly, render with audio and recover. Record unsupported face-level or translucent material editing as unmet, not as a pass; do not require external Blender or another external editing platform for the product workflow.

Record failed attempts, selected and rejected outputs, seed availability, generation and manual repair times, costs, hardware and peak VRAM only when actually measured. Small 2–3 case comparisons establish feasibility and specific failure examples, not population-wide equivalence or user satisfaction.

For a separately labelled best-native comparison, allow native multi-view or differing quality options only if their extra inputs, processing, costs, output and rendering conditions are disclosed; never merge the results into the same-condition comparison.
environment_needed: Rights-cleared inputs, including explicit likeness consent where relevant, a model/component dependency license review and permissible processing location.

Version-pinned TripoSG code, weights and preprocessing/texturing components, compatible CUDA hardware and disk space, and actual measured resources; do not assume model-card requirements prove available hardware or license clearance.

Commercial provider access and separately authorized costs/data transmission if comparison is later approved; capture whether the provider revision, seed and common single-view configuration can be controlled.

The current platform's working asset admission, scene editing, approval, save/reopen, rendering and recovery paths with verifiable receipts; material features outside its current support remain separate acceptance gaps.

A reproducible render scene and camera/light presets, source asset hashes and a rubric with task-specific pass criteria agreed before execution; actual practitioner evaluation separately, not simulated user feedback.
direct_benchmark_proposal.not_executed: No generation, model inference, mesh inspection, platform workflow run, practitioner evaluation, timing or cost measurement was performed in this review.

integrity_and_limits: Four local files were opened visually and their SHA-256 and byte counts recomputed against the existing sources.json; this verifies consistency with that manifest, not original authorship, independent publication authenticity or permission to use assets. Neither images nor the report establish distribution or commercial use rights. Existing research document remains unchanged.
